text: {"version":1,"kind":"conversation","reading":"The user is asking for a subjective recommendation on which player to build a team around, based on the previously returned 2017 per-game stats, not a new data query.","measures":[],"groupBy":[],"display":[],"filters":[],"expectedShape":"scalar","unresolved":[],"provenance":{},"reply":"That's a judgment call rather than something the data alone can answer, but here's how the three leaders compare on the stats we pulled: James Harden led in scoring (30.08 ppg) and was second in assists (9.79 apg) with modest rebounding (6.57 rpg) — the classic high-volume scorer/primary ball-handler profile. Russell Westbrook posted a near triple-double average (29.03/10.14/10.02) — the most well-rounded, do-everything stat line of the group. LeBron James was the most balanced high-efficiency player (28.20/8.76/8.70), contributing strongly in all three categories without being the outright leader in any. If you want a single primary scorer and playmaker to build an offense around, Harden's scoring plus elite assists make him the strongest choice. If you want a versatile two-way anchor who impacts rebounding, playmaking, and scoring equally, Westbrook or LeBron are better fits. Let me know if you'd like additional stats (efficiency, turnovers, wins) to make this comparison more rigorous."}
